question.ask: How many pieces are waiting in review?
question.whyItMatters: Dagny clears the review queue before scheduling.

text.text: Ideas get a script, scripts become drafts, drafts go to review, then get scheduled and published. Open the calendar to see the month; move cards on the board as work progresses.
The pipeline exists to answer one question: what is stuck, and who is it waiting on? Move a card only when the next person can start work.
Idea: capture it in the inbox with a score.
Scripting: write the outline, hook and call to action.
Drafting: one owner writes, records or shoots it.
Review: a second person checks facts and tone.
Scheduled: date and channel are locked.
A piece with no publish date cannot be scheduled. Pick the date when you move it to Drafting.
Nothing sits in Review for more than two days.
If a piece keeps missing its date, split it or drop the date until the script is done.
Published is only true once the asset link is saved.
YouTube: long how-tos and plant tours, one a week.
Instagram: carousels and reels that teach one thing.
TikTok: fast myths and behind-the-scenes clips.
LinkedIn: how the shop works, for wholesale buyers.
Blog and newsletter: searchable guides, the weekly email.
Run the same list for every channel. The items are boring on purpose, because the errors they prevent are the embarrassing kind.
